questions.stem: Gandhi's first nation-wide mass movement in India was against which British act, launched in 1919?

options.option_text: Rowlatt Act (Black Act) — allowed detention without trial

questions.explanation: ROWLATT ACT (Anarchical & Revolutionary Crimes Act, 1919) — based on Sidney Rowlatt's committee recommendations, allowed British to detain any 'suspected' person without trial for up to 2 years. Gandhi launched the ROWLATT SATYAGRAHA (March-April 1919) — his first all-India agitation. April 6, 1919: national hartal. The movement was violent in Punjab → JALLIANWALA BAGH MASSACRE (13 April 1919, Amritsar — Baisakhi day; Gen. Dyer shot unarmed crowd; 379+ killed officially). Tagore returned his knighthood in protest. Gandhi called off Rowlatt Satyagraha after violence (calling it his 'Himalayan blunder' — misjudging people's readiness for non-violence). This was the PRELUDE to the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920). Earlier satyagrahas in India: CHAMPARAN (1917, Bihar, Indigo farmers), KHEDA (1918, Gujarat, peasants), AHMEDABAD MILL (1918, textile workers).

questions.stem: The NON-COOPERATION MOVEMENT (Aug 1920 – Feb 1922) was SUSPENDED by Gandhi after which incident?

options.option_text: CHAURI CHAURA incident (5 Feb 1922, UP — 23 policemen burnt alive in police station)

questions.explanation: CHAURI CHAURA INCIDENT (5 February 1922, Gorakhpur district, UP): a non-cooperation procession was fired upon by police; protesters retaliated by setting the POLICE STATION ON FIRE, killing 22-23 policemen inside (plus 3 civilians shot). Gandhi, horrified by the violence (inconsistent with his non-violence principle), SUSPENDED the Non-Cooperation Movement on 12 February 1922 via the Bardoli Resolution of CWC. This was controversial — many (including Motilal Nehru, Subhas Bose, Jawaharlal) thought it was premature and demoralising. Gandhi was arrested 10 March 1922, tried for sedition (referring to his 'Young India' articles), given 6 years (imprisoned at Yeravda, Pune; released 1924 for appendicitis surgery). His famous trial 'Great Trial of 1922'. NCM's positives: mass mobilisation; boycott of goods, schools, titles; ~30k arrests.

questions.stem: The DANDI MARCH / SALT SATYAGRAHA — launched by Gandhi as part of the Civil Disobedience Movement — covered how many days, what distance, and violated which specific British law?

options.option_text: 12 days; 240 km from Sabarmati to Dandi; broke the Salt Law by making salt from seawater
24 days; 240 miles (~386 km); broke the Salt Act 1882 (which gave British monopoly on salt production + imposed salt tax)
10 days; 100 km; broke the Rowlatt Act

questions.explanation: DANDI MARCH (SALT SATYAGRAHA): Started 12 MARCH 1930 from SABARMATI ASHRAM (Ahmedabad), ended 6 APRIL 1930 at DANDI, a coastal village in Navsari, Gujarat. DURATION: 24 days. DISTANCE: 240 MILES (~386 km). 78 initial marchers; tens of thousands joined en route. At Dandi, Gandhi picked up a handful of salt-encrusted mud on the beach and symbolically violated the SALT ACT 1882 (which gave the British govt a monopoly on salt production + taxed salt — a burden on the poor). Sparked the full CIVIL DISOBEDIENCE MOVEMENT (1930-34). Salt-making spread across India. Accompanying events: Abbas Tyabji + Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana Salt March (May 1930, after Gandhi's arrest — British brutally beat unarmed satyagrahis; global press coverage by Webb Miller). Gandhi jailed 5 May 1930. RELEASED via GANDHI-IRWIN PACT (5 March 1931). Dandi's original name 'Dandi Kutir' memorialised Salt Satyagraha site today.

questions.stem: The PURNA SWARAJ resolution was adopted by the Indian National Congress at the:

options.option_text: 1929 LAHORE session under Jawaharlal Nehru's presidency

questions.explanation: PURNA SWARAJ (Complete Independence) resolution was passed at the LAHORE SESSION of INC in December 1929, with JAWAHARLAL NEHRU (at 40, youngest-ever INC President) presiding. At midnight of 31 December 1929, on the banks of the Ravi river, the tricolour was unfurled — declaring Purna Swaraj as the political goal of India (previously 'Dominion Status' was considered enough, per the Motilal Nehru Report 1928). 26 JANUARY 1930 was declared PURNA SWARAJ DIWAS — celebrated annually as Independence Day until 1947. When independence came (15 Aug 1947), 26 January was kept as REPUBLIC DAY to honour this legacy (Constitution came into force 26 Jan 1950). The Lahore session authorised Civil Disobedience Movement — launched via Dandi March 1930. Declaration of Purna Swaraj was drafted by Gandhi.

questions.stem: The GANDHI-IRWIN PACT (March 1931) paved the way for Gandhi's participation in which event?

options.option_text: SECOND Round Table Conference (London, 1931) as sole Congress representative

questions.explanation: GANDHI-IRWIN PACT (5 March 1931) — signed between Gandhi and VICEROY LORD IRWIN. Key terms: (1) Congress called off CDM; (2) British released all political prisoners NOT guilty of violence; (3) Peaceful picketing + making salt near the coast allowed; (4) Gandhi agreed to attend the Second Round Table Conference. ROUND TABLE CONFERENCES (London): (1) FIRST — Nov 1930 to Jan 1931, NO Congress (Gandhi/CDM continuing); (2) SECOND — Sept-Dec 1931, Gandhi attended as SOLE Congress representative; (3) THIRD — Nov-Dec 1932, Congress again absent (Gandhi + CWC in jail). The 2nd RTC saw the DEMAND FOR SEPARATE ELECTORATES for Dalits (proposed by Dr. Ambedkar), leading to the COMMUNAL AWARD 1932 by Ramsay MacDonald, which Gandhi opposed (violently — his famous FAST UNTO DEATH at Yeravda jail resulted in the POONA PACT, 24 Sept 1932, between Gandhi + Ambedkar — reserved seats in joint electorate instead).

questions.stem: The POONA PACT (24 Sept 1932) was signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to resolve the issue of:

options.option_text: Separate electorates for Depressed Classes (Dalits) — replaced with reserved seats in joint electorate
Permission for Gandhi to meet Viceroy

questions.explanation: POONA PACT (Yerwada Jail, Pune — 24 September 1932) — between Gandhi + Ambedkar. Background: Ramsay MacDonald's COMMUNAL AWARD (16 Aug 1932) granted SEPARATE ELECTORATES to Depressed Classes (Dalits). Gandhi vehemently opposed — saying it would divide Hindu society permanently — began his 'fast unto death' (20 Sept 1932) at Yerwada jail where he was imprisoned. After 6 days of national tension, Dr. AMBEDKAR agreed to withdraw separate electorates in exchange for: (1) RESERVED SEATS (148 instead of original 71) for Depressed Classes within the JOINT ELECTORATE; (2) Primary electorate (by Dalits) → 4 candidates → final election by all. Became the foundation of caste-based reservations in post-Independence India. Ambedkar later expressed ambivalence about this compromise (felt pressured). The pact was ratified by British PM. This issue foreshadowed Ambedkar's later conversion to Buddhism (1956).

questions.stem: Gandhi's concept of 'SATYAGRAHA' (non-violent resistance) was first developed during his 21-year stay in:
questions.explanation: GANDHI'S SOUTH AFRICA years (1893-1914, age 24-45) — 21 years spent here, where he developed SATYAGRAHA (from satya = truth, agraha = insistence). Key moments: (1) 1893 — thrown off Pietermaritzburg train for being in first class despite ticket → politicised him. (2) 1906 — Johannesburg: 'Asiatic Law Amendment Ordinance' required Indians to register fingerprints — Gandhi launched first SATYAGRAHA; called 'passive resistance' then. (3) 1913 — Newcastle: led miners' strike against poll tax on Indians. Arrested multiple times. (4) Returned to India 9 January 1915 (celebrated today as 'Pravasi Bharatiya Divas'). Advised by GOPAL KRISHNA GOKHALE ('political guru') to travel India before jumping into politics. Early influences: Tolstoy, Ruskin ('Unto This Last'), Thoreau's civil disobedience, Jain + Hindu + Christian teachings. Gandhi's South African autobiography 'SATYAGRAHA IN SOUTH AFRICA' (1928).

questions.stem: The CIVIL DISOBEDIENCE MOVEMENT (1930-34) was suspended formally through the GANDHI-IRWIN PACT (1931), later resumed in 1932, and finally called off in 1934. Which of the following was a prominent WOMAN leader during this movement?

options.option_text: Sarojini Naidu (led Dharasana Salt March after Gandhi's arrest)
Annie Besant (died 1933, mostly removed from active politics)

questions.explanation: WOMEN IN CDM: SAROJINI NAIDU ('Nightingale of India') — led the Dharasana Salt March (May 1930) after Gandhi was arrested, facing British police beatings captured by American journalist Webb Miller whose reports shocked global opinion. KASTURBA GANDHI — picketed liquor shops + foreign cloth shops. KAMALA NEHRU (Jawaharlal's wife). MOTILAL NEHRU's wife SWARUPRANI, and daughters Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit + Krishna Hutheesing. ARUNA ASAF ALI (later famous for 1942 Quit India — hoisted flag at Gowalia Tank). MATANGINI HAZRA (Bengal, shot dead carrying tricolour 1942). DURGAWATI DEVI (Durga Bhabhi — revolutionary, helped Bhagat Singh escape). BASANTI DEVI (C.R. Das's wife). KAMALADEVI CHATTOPADHYAY (first woman to stand for Legislative Assembly). MOST OF THESE became active from 1920s NCM onwards — CDM saw unprecedented female participation.

questions.stem: The CHAMPARAN SATYAGRAHA (1917) — Gandhi's first satyagraha in INDIA — was against:

options.option_text: The oppressive TINKATHIA system imposed on indigo cultivators in Bihar

questions.explanation: CHAMPARAN SATYAGRAHA (April 1917, Champaran district, Bihar). Gandhi, barely 2 years back from SA, was summoned by RAJ KUMAR SHUKLA — a local peasant leader — to investigate the plight of INDIGO CULTIVATORS. British planters forced farmers to grow INDIGO on 3/20 (TINKATHIA SYSTEM) of their land and sell it at fixed low prices. When synthetic dyes made indigo uneconomic (~1890s), planters pressed farmers harder + demanded 'tavan' compensation. Gandhi conducted survey, was ordered to leave Champaran — REFUSED — was arrested → local mass support → British backed down. Outcome: CHAMPARAN AGRARIAN ACT (1918) abolished Tinkathia + refunded a portion of illegal exactions. Gandhi's colleagues: RAJENDRA PRASAD (later 1st President of India!), J.B. Kripalani, Brajkishore Prasad, Mahadev Desai, Anugrah Narayan Sinha. This was Gandhi's FIRST ALL-INDIA political triumph using Satyagraha. Later satyagrahas: KHEDA (1918, against high land revenue during bad crops, Gujarat), AHMEDABAD MILL WORKERS (1918, wage strike).

questions.stem: Gandhi's KHILAFAT MOVEMENT alliance (1919-1924) aligned the Indian National Congress with Muslim leaders to protest:

options.option_text: The British dismantling of the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I

questions.explanation: KHILAFAT MOVEMENT (1919-1924) — a pan-Islamic movement by Indian Muslims to protest the British proposal (after WWI) to dismember the OTTOMAN EMPIRE + reduce the status of the Caliph (Khalifa — the spiritual head of Sunni Islam, historically the Ottoman Sultan). Led by the ALI BROTHERS (Muhammad Ali + Shaukat Ali), Maulana Azad, Hakim Ajmal Khan, Hasrat Mohani. GANDHI supported it strongly — saw it as opportunity for HINDU-MUSLIM UNITY — merged Khilafat with the NON-COOPERATION MOVEMENT (1920). Khilafat Committee + Congress joint campaign. The movement COLLAPSED when: (1) Chauri Chaura led Gandhi to suspend NCM in 1922; (2) TURKEY itself (Mustafa Kemal Atatürk) ABOLISHED the Caliphate in 1924, ending the movement's raison d'être. Aftermath: communal riots, Moplah uprising (Kerala, 1921, peasant + Khilafat), eventual break in Hindu-Muslim political unity. Some argue this alliance indirectly strengthened pan-Islamic identity, contributing to later demand for Pakistan.
